wrong: Place where the vehicles came to rest
That is the final rest position, reached after the collision.
Spot where the driver first saw danger
That is the point of perception, which comes before the impact.
Point where braking first began
That is where the skid starts, before the collision.
Measure of tire tread depth
Tread depth affects grip, but the coefficient of friction compares the friction force with the weight on the surface.
Rate of change of speed
That is acceleration or deceleration.
Measure of road slope
That is the grade of the road.
Measuring skid marks to estimate speed
That is skid mark analysis.
Measuring crush depth to estimate speed
That is crush (damage) analysis.
Timing the traffic signal cycle at the scene
Signal timing may be checked, but it is not momentum analysis.
Measuring skid length to determine stopping distance
That is skid mark analysis.
Measuring tire marks to determine vehicle direction
That is tire mark analysis, not the study of vehicle deformation.
Measuring glass fragments to locate the impact point
That uses glass debris, not the crush damage on the vehicles.
Photograph, sketch, note, collect
Those are documentation and collection steps, not search methods.
Inner, outer and extended perimeters
Those are scene perimeters (cordons), not search patterns.
Survey, search, seal, release
Those are general stages of processing a scene, not the search methods.
Every crime has a motive and opportunity
Motive and opportunity are investigative concepts, not Locard's principle.
Evidence is lost as time passes
That happens in practice, but it is not Locard's Exchange Principle.
No two fingerprints are ever alike
That is the principle of individuality of fingerprints, not Locard's.
Typing blood to group possible sources
That is serology (blood typing).
Extracting DNA profiles from blood samples
That is DNA analysis.
Testing stains to confirm they are blood
That is presumptive or confirmatory blood testing.
Searching in parallel lanes across the scene
That is the strip (line) method.
Searching in overlapping lanes in two directions
That is the grid (double strip) method.
Searching pie-shaped sections from the center
That is the wheel (ray) method.
Recording the scene by photograph and sketch
That is documentation, which reconstruction relies on but is not.
Securing the scene to keep people out
That is scene protection.
Collecting and packaging physical evidence
That is evidence collection.
Physical evidence cannot lie
A saying about the reliability of evidence (attributed to Kirk), not Locard's Exchange Principle.
The scene must be secured first
That is a rule of scene management, not Locard's principle.
Trace evidence is always visible
False, and not the principle: much trace evidence is microscopic.
Study of offenders and the causes of their crimes
That is criminology (criminal etiology).
Study of how police respond to reported crimes
That is police science.
Study of laws that define crimes and penalties
That is criminal law.
Comparing DNA from the scene with suspects
That is DNA analysis.
Matching latent prints from the crime scene
That is fingerprint comparison.
Interviewing witnesses about what they saw
That is witness interviewing.
Investigation of a death ruled a homicide
When a death is clearly a homicide, it is not equivocal.
Investigation of deaths in police custody
Custodial deaths have their own procedures; 'equivocal' means the manner of death is uncertain.
Examination of a body to find the time of death
That is estimating the postmortem interval.
Scene left untouched by the offender
That is an undisturbed scene, the opposite of staging.
Scene contaminated by first responders
Contamination is accidental; staging is deliberate deception by the offender.
Scene recreated to train investigators
That is a mock scene for training.
Network of persons who distribute illegal drugs
That is a distribution network, not chain of custody.
Laboratory test that confirms a drug's identity
That is the confirmatory test. Chain of custody documents who handled the evidence, and when.
Order in which suspects are arrested in a buy-bust
The order of arrests is not chain of custody.
Explosive burning when air enters suddenly
That is backdraft.
Flames rolling across the ceiling layer
That is rollover (flameover), which can come before flashover.
Point where the fire first started
That is the point of origin.
Burn patterns showing liquid was poured
Those are pour patterns. A V-pattern narrows toward where the fire started.
Soot patterns showing smoke movement
Smoke deposits are a different kind of pattern; the V-pattern points to the origin.
Cracks in glass caused by heat
That is heat crazing or fracture of glass.
Arrest the suspect before collecting evidence
Arrest timing depends on the case. The golden rule is about not disturbing evidence before it is documented.
Interview witnesses before anything else
Witnesses matter, but the golden rule is about the physical evidence.
Release the scene once evidence is bagged
That is the end of processing, not the golden rule.
Interview method to improve witness recall
That is the cognitive interview.
Information gathering model without accusation
That is the PEACE model, often contrasted with the Reid Technique.
Polygraph method for detecting deception
The polygraph is a separate, instrument-based technique.
Recording each transfer of physical evidence
That is chain of custody.
Protecting witnesses who testify in court
That is witness protection.
Ranking crimes by seriousness for patrol
That is prioritization, not linkage analysis.
Reviewing a single case file in detail
That is case review, not pattern analysis.
Profiling the personality of one offender
That is criminal profiling.
Planning the police budget for the year
That is budget planning.
Responding to calls only after crimes occur
That is reactive policing.
Partnering with residents to solve problems
That is community-oriented policing.
Patrolling at random to deter offenders
That is random preventive patrol.

Investigation of firearm evidence
That is forensic ballistics.
Investigation of document forgeries
That is questioned document examination.
Investigation of fire origins
That is arson investigation.
Operational Security Intelligence
OSINT means Open Source Intelligence: information from publicly available sources.
Official Secret Information
OSINT means Open Source Intelligence: information from publicly available sources.
Offline Surveillance Intelligence
OSINT means Open Source Intelligence: information from publicly available sources.
Signals intelligence from intercepted messages
That is SIGINT. HUMINT comes from people, such as informants and contacts.
Imagery intelligence from photos and satellites
That is IMINT. HUMINT comes from people, such as informants and contacts.
Open source intelligence from public media
That is OSINT. HUMINT comes from people, such as informants and contacts.
Accusatory technique for gaining confessions
That is accusatory interrogation, such as the Reid Technique.
Instrument test for detecting deception
That is the polygraph.
Lineup procedure for identifying suspects
That is an identification lineup.
Locating an offender's likely home base on a map
That is geographic profiling.
Matching DNA from the scene to a database
That is DNA database searching.
Determining the cause of death by autopsy
That is forensic pathology.
Tracking a suspect's phone through GPS signals
That is location tracking, not geographic profiling.
Mapping where all crimes in a city happen
That is crime mapping (hot spots). Geo-profiling estimates where one serial offender likely lives.
Portrait of an unknown offender's personality
That is criminal (psychological) profiling.
Estimating the money lost to a crime
That is loss assessment.
Ranking areas by their recorded crime rate
That is crime analysis, not threat assessment.
Checking whether a suspect is lying
That is deception detection.
Checking a written statement for grammar errors
Grammar is not the point; statement analysis looks for signs of deception in the wording.
Comparing handwriting to identify the writer
That is handwriting (questioned document) examination.
Recording a suspect's answers on a polygraph
That is polygraph testing.
Team processing physical evidence at scenes
That is the scene of the crime (SOCO) unit.
Team negotiating with hostage takers
That is the crisis negotiation team.
Team handling internal police discipline
That is internal affairs.
Measuring vehicle speeds at a road point
That is a spot speed study.
Timing trips between two points on a road
That is a travel time study.
Recording where vehicles start and end trips
That is an origin-destination study.
Study of how many vehicles pass a point
That is a traffic volume study.
Study of where accidents happen most
That is crash location (black spot) analysis.
Study of drivers' reaction times
That is human factors research.
Simulator training for new drivers
Driving simulators train drivers; traffic simulation models how traffic flows.
Crash testing of vehicles in a laboratory
That is vehicle crash testing.
Manual counting of vehicles at a junction
That is a traffic volume count.
Measure of police response time
That is response time, a police performance measure.
Measure of road pavement condition
That is a pavement condition rating.
Measure of accidents per kilometer
That is a crash rate.
Convicted within ten years of release, a third time or more
That is habitual delinquency (Art. 62): a third or later conviction for certain crimes within ten years.
Committing a new felony while serving sentence
That is quasi-recidivism (Art. 160).
Previously punished for an offense with an equal or greater penalty
That is reiteracion or habituality (Art. 14(10)), which does not require the same title of the Code.
